index.title: Free workout programs
index.intro: Complete programs with every workout, exercise, set and rep written out. Read one here, or open it in Musclog with one tap and start training. Starting weights are suggested from your own profile when you open it in the app.

detail.openBody: This opens the program in the app as a review, so nothing is saved until you confirm. Starting weights are suggested from your profile, and you choose the weekdays. If you do not have the app yet, the next page has the download links.
how: Do the workouts in order and repeat the cycle. One workout per training day is the simplest way to run it; the order matters more than the weekday.
Start with weights you can lift with good form and a couple of reps left. When you reach the top of the rep range on every set, add weight next time.
These programs are general examples, not medical advice. If you have an injury or a health condition, check with a professional first.

summaries.push-pull-legs: Three workouts: push (chest, shoulders and triceps), pull (back and biceps) and legs. Run the three once a week, or go through them twice for the classic six-day version.
summaries.upper-lower-4-day: Four workouts: two upper-body days and two lower-body days, which trains each muscle twice a week on a four-day schedule.
summaries.full-body-3-day: Three full-body workouts for beginners. Each one has a leg movement, a press, a pull and some arm work, so every muscle is trained three times a week.
summaries.phul: Four workouts: two upper and two lower. The first of each pair is a heavy power day with low reps, the second is a hypertrophy day with higher reps.
summaries.5-day-hypertrophy-split: Five workouts, one area each: chest, back, shoulders, legs and arms. More volume per muscle in a session, one hard session per muscle a week.
summaries.arnold-split: Three workouts in the Arnold style: chest and back, shoulders and arms, then legs. The split is traditionally run twice through, for six training days.
summaries.bro-split: Five workouts, one muscle group each: chest, back, legs, shoulders and arms. Each muscle gets one focused session a week.
summaries.2-day-full-body: Two full-body workouts, A and B, for weeks when you can only train twice. Alternate them.
summaries.3-day-strength-builder: Three workouts built around heavier sets of 4 to 8 reps on the squat, bench press, deadlift and rows, with lighter accessory work after them.
summaries.classic-3-day-split: Three workouts: chest and triceps, back and biceps, then legs and shoulders. A classic split for a three-day week.
summaries.brolic-workout: Two upper-body workouts, chest and shoulders, with plenty of pressing and fly work. Shorter than most programs here.
summaries.cable-superset-workout: Five advanced workouts (Upper A, Lower A, Arms, Upper B, Lower B) built from cable exercises, paired in antagonist supersets, with a rep range and a rest time for each exercise.
summaries.short-full-body-gym: Two short full-body workouts, A and B, on gym machines and free weights: about 30 minutes, 2 sets each, easy on purpose. A good way back after a break.
summaries.short-full-body-home: Two short full-body workouts, A and B, with dumbbells, a kettlebell and bands: about 30 minutes, 2 sets each, easy on purpose.
summaries.short-full-body-no-equipment: Two short full-body workouts, A and B, with just your body and a band: about 30 minutes, 2 sets each, easy on purpose.
